title: eMudhra Intermediate CA Compromise
summary:
Private keys for eight eMudhra intermediate CA certificates have been compromised, allowing attackers to forge certificates for any site. The keys were revealed due to low entropy, not through a known breach. Browsers blocked them using revocation lists, but other software had to remove the emSign ECC G3 root. Unpatched systems remain exposed to forged certificates, including client auth and mTLS.

By Chris Swan

title: Netflix Bridges AWS IAM and Internal Identity with Workload Attestation
summary:
Netflix has developed a workload attestation mechanism for Apache Spark jobs running on Amazon EMR. The design combines AWS IAM identity with signed claims from Netflix’s control plane before issuing short-lived internal X.509 certificates, allowing managed compute workloads to authenticate to internal services without directly injecting credentials.

By Leela Kumili

title: Article: Distributed Spring Batch Without a Message Broker
summary:
Distributed Spring Batch partitioning already needs a shared, persistent job repository. This article makes that database the whole coordination plane and drops the message broker, sizing work to the live node count, a per-job master with no standing coordinator, compare-and-set claiming that prevents double-execution, two-phase heartbeat failover, and where a broker is still the right choice.

By Janardhan Reddy Chejarla

title: Cilium 1.20 Expands Gateway API and Opens eBPF Datapath for Kubernetes
summary:
Cilium 1.20 has been released with broader Kubernetes Gateway API support, an extensible eBPF datapath and further work on sidecarless mutual TLS. The release also makes the newer netkit network device easier to introduce across Kubernetes fleets that run different Linux kernel versions.

By Matt Saunders

title: Microsoft Previews dotnetup: Toolchain Manager for .NET SDKs and Runtimes
summary:
Microsoft has released a public preview of dotnetup, a cross-platform toolchain manager that installs and updates .NET SDKs and runtimes in the user’s own directory without admin rights. It tracks channels such as latest, lts, preview, and daily, reads global.json, and removes unused installs. Commands may still change before general availability.

By Almir Vuk

title: TornadoVM 7 Enables GPU-Native Workloads From Java Applications
summary:
TornadoVM, an open-source heterogeneous programming framework for Java has reached version 7.0. It automatically accelerates Java programs on multi-core CPUs and GPUs and provides a rich GPU programming ecosystem in Java that can be used with any mainstream JDK distribution e.g. Temurin, Red Hat OpenJDK, Coretto, Oracle, GraalVM or Zulu.

By Ben Evans

title: Pinterest Uses Event Time Watermarks to Finalize Petabyte Scale Data Partitions
summary:
Pinterest has introduced event time-based partition finalization for its database ingestion framework. The mechanism uses Apache Flink to track event time and Apache Iceberg metadata to publish a non-regressing watermark, helping downstream jobs determine when continuously ingested CDC data is sufficiently complete for processing.

By Leela Kumili

title: JEP 543 Finalizes Structured Concurrency in JDK 28, Ending Seven Preview Rounds
summary:
JDK 28 finalizes structured concurrency through JEP 543, with no API changes from JDK 27. Teams on JDK 27 only need to drop --enable-preview and recompile. Code written for JDK 25 or 26 must adapt to the R_X exception type parameter, ExecutionException wrapping, and the abstract timeout() joiner callback.

By A N M Bazlur Rahman

title: Article: From Microservices to Agents: the Next Evolution of Distributed Systems
summary:
The article examines the transition from microservices to agentic AI architecture in distributed systems. Microservices allow for functional decomposition, while agentic systems focus on decision decomposition. This shift introduces new complexities in observability, reliability, and system design, highlighting the need for updated architectural patterns and practices.

By Mallika Rao
